chunks: And when they entered upon Joseph, he brought his brother close to him and said: 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not grieve for what they used to do.'

key_terms.آوَى: He made close / he brought near
key_terms.تَبْتَئِسْ: Do not grieve / do not be sad

ai.seo_question: How did Joseph comfort his brother Benjamin when they met in Egypt?
ai.summary: In this pivotal moment, Joseph reveals his identity to Benjamin, his full brother, while the other brothers remain unaware, fulfilling the divine plan of gradual revelation. Shia scholars often highlight this as a moment of *sabr* (patience) and *tawhid* in action, where Joseph’s elevation is not merely political but a spiritual test for his brothers to recognize their shared lineage and divine mercy. The phrase 'do not grieve' (*la tabtas*) serves as a theological reassurance that their past sins do not negate God's ultimate wisdom in preserving the progeny of Jacob.
